title: Why radiotherapy aims from many angles
body: Radiotherapy uses radiation to treat cancer. External beam radiotherapy comes from a machine that aims radiation at the cancer.
Dose means how much radiation a spot receives. A beam gives a dose to every spot on its path, including healthy tissue.
Radiation can also affect nearby healthy cells. Damage to healthy cells can cause side effects.
So the machine can move around the person. It sends radiation from many directions.
Each weaker beam has very little effect on the tissue it passes through. Where all the beams meet, the doses add up.
The treatment team plans this carefully. They aim to give a high dose to the cancer while sparing as much healthy tissue as possible.
realWorld: This crossfire idea is why a radiotherapy machine moves around the person during treatment.
model: This is a teaching model. Its doses are made-up scores shown as colour, not real radiation doses.
